entities.summary:
Ford Motor Company is an American multinational automobile manufacturer founded in 1903 by Henry Ford in Detroit, Michigan. Ford's invention of the moving assembly line at the Highland Park plant in 1913 created mass production as we know it, reducing the price of the Model T to make automobiles accessible to the American working class and transforming industrial civilization.

Henry Ford's double revolution — the moving assembly line and the $5 workday (1914) — simultaneously slashed production costs and raised workers' wages enough to buy the products they made, creating the consumer economy. The Model T, produced from 1908 to 1927, put America on wheels: ownership rose from 1 in 650 Americans in 1900 to 1 in 5 by 1920. Ford became an international phenomenon, with plants opening in Britain, Germany, and Australia.

Ford's 20th-century highlights included the Mustang (1964), which created the 'pony car' segment, and the F-Series pickup truck, America's best-selling vehicle for 46 consecutive years. The company's 2020s pivot to electric vehicles — including the F-150 Lightning and Mustang Mach-E — represents its latest adaptation. Henry Ford's personal antisemitism and publication of 'The International Jew' cast a shadow over his industrial legacy but did not diminish his manufacturing innovations' global impact.
